title: MNS Suporte
html:
MNS Suporte is the MNS internal IT support channel for opening, consulting, and following GLPI tickets from WhatsApp. The product scope defines the guided V1 workflow and the boundary for future AI assistance.

Current state

This repository was initialized on 2026-11-25 from Orion commit 6fe8aa850d9fc3d8e78584c6f4af27d524e3ac75. It contains the foundation's architecture, policies, accepted ADRs, tooling, validation gate, CI, generated references, and internal Living Documentation Portal, and the neutral web shell. The API verifies official Meta WhatsApp webhooks, persists inbound messages and dispatches queued replies with delivery tracking. The GLPI adapter supports exact active-user lookup and a guarded single ticket-creation attempt. The product plan tracks conversation processing and the live pilot. The complete portal remains available in local development; production builds exclude it and its generated assets by default. Product help and public API documentation require separately approved sources and application-owned presentation under the documentation policy. The planned employee identity flow verifies access to the corporate mailbox.

The project plan and project human actions own this repository's current work and external prerequisites. The project manifest records the project identity, the immutable initialization commit, and the Orion baseline currently integrated. Project derivation explains how to inspect provenance and adopt newer Orion revisions through reviewed merges.

Accepted architecture and implemented capability are different states. Consult the technology map for selected directions and deliberately deferred choices, and validation availability for current checks. With Node.js 24.13.0 and pnpm 11.25.0, follow the canonical development setup for installation, local environment loading, execution, and the full gate.

Directory trees in architecture documents describe intended responsibilities, not proof that those directories exist. The physical repository takes precedence over illustrations. English is the canonical repository language; product localization is separate.
